Defense Budget Lab, FY2026 and FY2027

Selected weapon systems, personnel pay, and what a change to one would cost

By Alyssa I. Agard

Fiscal year 2027

What the request asks for, and what the committees did to it

Every figure traces to a page

Each line carries the CRS table it came from, the page it was printed on, and the footnote attached to it. A blank means CRS printed nothing there. It is never shown as a zero.

Written instructions, priced

Type an instruction the way you would say it to a staffer. The composer reads it, prices it against the baseline you choose, and shows the offset it implies.

Two years, one spine

The FY2026 and FY2027 reports do not use the same column names. The crosswalk says which pairs are comparable, and where a programme appears in only one year it stays blank rather than reading as a cut.

Context

The selected systems inside the whole request

Scenario composer

Write the change, and see what it costs

One instruction a line. The parser understands add, cut, set, and zero, in dollars or in percentages, against a named system, a category, a service, or the whole portfolio. Add an offset clause and the money is taken from somewhere.

Line by line

Claim tester

Put a number in proportion

A figure on its own says little. This takes a change and expresses it four ways: as a share of its own line, as units of the thing it buys, as a cut somewhere else, and as an across-the-board military pay raise. The change can be a percentage of a line CRS printed, an amount you type in any unit from dollars to trillions, or a claim of your own that appears in neither report.

The data

Every line CRS printed

Click a column heading to sort. A blank cell means CRS printed no figure on that line. It is not a zero and it is not a cut.

Method

How this was built, and where it disagrees with itself

Every figure on this page is read from the workbook. Nothing is recomputed here, and no figure is adjusted to make a total come out. Where a computed total and a figure CRS states in its own narrative disagree, both are shown and the gap is named.
